reviews.reason: The entire unit, including its continuation before verse 2, has been assessed. The existing English omits both the bracketed Ethiopic interpolation and the separate final completion clause. The draft's connection of sinners and the wicked to that clause remains unresolved; the English below is a provisional editorial proposal, not publication approval or human certification.
reviews.suggested_text: From the days of the slaughter, destruction, and death of the giants,[a] the spirits that came forth from the souls of their flesh[b] shall destroy without judgment;[c] thus they shall destroy until the day of the completion of the great judgment, when the great age shall be brought to its end.[d] [Concerning sinners and the wicked,][e] all shall be completed.[f]
reviews.footnote_changes:
[a] “The giants” identifies those whose slaughter, destruction, and death are described; it does not identify the Watchers as the slain.
[b] This wording follows Charles’s critically edited Ethiopic text. His apparatus records emendations in the wording concerning the spirits and their destructive activity; it is not an unqualified transcription of a single manuscript.
[c] Literally, “without judgment.” “Without incurring judgment” is an interpretive expansion. The phrase must not be understood as a promise that these spirits will never face judgment.
[d] The great judgment and the ending of the great age belong to the preceding completion statement. The following bracketed words and final completion clause are additional printed material, not replacements for this statement.
[e] Charles identifies the bracketed material as an Ethiopic interpolation. “Concerning sinners and the wicked” is a tentative English connection, not a settled rendering of its syntax. The Greek parallels do not contain this interpolation; its relationship to the following clause remains uncertain.
[f] The final completion clause must be retained separately. Charles critically marks “all”; his apparatus reports omission of this clause in m and β and cites the additional completion wording in the Greek witness Gˢ as support.

reviews.reason: The draft appropriately preserves the introductory fragment. Retain that structure and add a note explaining the absence of an explicit speech verb. Do not turn the commission into a newly narrated delivery of the message.
reviews.suggested_text: And now, as for the Watchers who sent you to petition on their behalf, who formerly were in heaven:[a]
reviews.footnote_changes: [a] The printed Ethiopic has no explicit verb such as “say” or “tell” in this introductory fragment. The colon connects it to the address that follows; it does not imply that Enoch has now delivered the message.

reviews.reason: Preserve the bracketed opening, parenthesized “all,” and critically marked negative rather than smoothing them into an unqualified sentence. “Despised” is closer to the Ethiopic mystery word than the interpretive “worthless.” Keep women as the recipients of the disclosure and women and men as the subjects of the subsequent increase of evil.
reviews.suggested_text: [And now,][a] you were in heaven, but not yet had (all)[b] the hidden things been revealed to you.[c] You knew a despised mystery,[d] and you made this known to women in the hardness of your hearts; through this mystery women and men multiplied evil upon the earth.[e]
reviews.footnote_changes:
[a] Charles brackets “And now” and identifies it as an Ethiopic interpolation.
[b] “All” is parenthesized and critically starred in Charles’s printed text. His apparatus states that he added it in accordance with the Greek. It should not be presented as an independently established Ethiopic manuscript reading.
[c] The negative is critically marked in the printed Ethiopic. This translation follows that editorially marked reading and retains “not yet”; the resulting sentence is not an unqualified manuscript reading.
[d] “A despised mystery” follows the Ethiopic wording. “Worthless” would interpret its significance. The Greek main text differs, describing a mystery originating from God; Charles’s Greek apparatus identifies the Ethiopic counterpart as “despised.” The Greek wording has not been substituted into this translation.
[e] The disclosure is made to women. In the ensuing clause, women and men multiply evil upon the earth. “Hardness of your hearts” describes the Watchers’ disposition; it must not be reassigned to the human recipients.

reviews.reason: The proposed English preserves the command and its judgment correctly. Add an explicit recipient note so that “no peace” is not broadened into a pronouncement against all humanity. No pardon or reconciliation clause is present.
reviews.suggested_text: Tell them, therefore, “You have no peace.”[a]
reviews.footnote_changes: [a] “Them” refers to the Watchers introduced in verse 2 and addressed in verse 3. The declaration of no peace is directed to them, not to humanity generally.
